- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

# andesim driver: a standalone C++20 executable.
#
# Intentionally minimal -- no Verilator, no SystemC, no QEMU, no fmt/spdlog.
# It depends only on the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header at
# include/hybrid/state_abi.h (consumed from F5 on for state-file reads).
#
# Build out-of-tree via scripts/build_driver.sh, which points
# CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY at the repo's build/ so the binary lands at
# build/andesim.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(andes_sim CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

add_executable(andesim
  main.cpp
  cli.cpp
  cmd_list.cpp
  cmd_doctor.cpp
  cmd_run.cpp
  hybrid.cpp
  elf_syms.cpp
  process.cpp
  shm.cpp
  argv.cpp
  run_plan.cpp
  run_passthrough.cpp
  vsim_filter.cpp
  engine_registry.cpp
  state_diff.cpp
)

# Shared ABI header lives at <repo>/include/hybrid/state_abi.h, two levels up.
target_include_directories(andesim PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(andesim PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)

# Unit tests. Kept in the build tree (build/driver), not redirected to build/,
# so build/ holds only the shipped binary.
add_executable(andesim-cli-test cli_test.cpp cli.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-json-test json_test.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-infra-test infra_test.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
add_executable(andesim-plan-test plan_test.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp)
# F6 integration acceptance: spawns real qemu+vsim, so it also needs the registry.
add_executable(andesim-plan-itest plan_itest.cpp argv.cpp run_plan.cpp process.cpp shm.cpp engine_registry.cpp)
# F7 transparent-passthrough argv assembly (pure; no spawn).
add_executable(andesim-run-test run_test.cpp run_passthrough.cpp argv.cpp process.cpp)
# cycle-mode output filter: banner/[info] suppression + cycle-count lift (pure).
add_executable(andesim-vsimfilter-test vsim_filter_test.cpp vsim_filter.cpp)
# F9 pc-trigger boundary resolver (pure; reads a fixture ELF's .symtab).
add_executable(andesim-elf-syms-test elf_syms_test.cpp elf_syms.cpp)
# F9 hybrid trigger build (pure; resolves pc boundaries against a fixture ELF).
add_executable(andesim-hybrid-test hybrid_test.cpp hybrid.cpp elf_syms.cpp cli.cpp)
# verify_oracle F2: the oracle differential compare (pure; synthetic states).
add_executable(andesim-state-diff-test state_diff_test.cpp state_diff.cpp)
# EX1: vsim scan dir picks $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim, mirrors $QEMU_BIN_DIR).
add_executable(andesim-engine-registry-test engine_registry_test.cpp engine_registry.cpp process.cpp)

# hotloops: C++ replacement for QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh.
add_executable(hotloops hotloops.cpp elf_syms.cpp process.cpp)
target_include_directories(hotloops PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_compile_options(hotloops PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
set_target_properties(hotloops PROPERTIES
  RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY})
foreach(_t andesim-cli-test andesim-json-test andesim-infra-test andesim-plan-test andesim-plan-itest andesim-run-test andesim-vsimfilter-test andesim-elf-syms-test andesim-hybrid-test andesim-state-diff-test andesim-engine-registry-test)
  target_compile_options(${_t} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra)
  set_target_properties(${_t} PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
endforeach()
# infra/plan tests read hybrid_state_v1 via state.hpp, which includes the shared ABI.
target_include_directories(andesim-infra-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-plan-itest PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
target_include_directories(andesim-state-diff-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
# hybrid-test reaches plan.hpp via hybrid.hpp; plan.hpp carries the drained
# record (hybrid_state_v1) since verify_oracle F4.
target_include_directories(andesim-hybrid-test PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../include)
----BUILD_DRIVER----
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the andesim driver: driver/ -> build/andesim.
#
# Standalone C++20 target (no Verilator, SystemC, or QEMU). Depends only on
# the host C++ toolchain and the shared ABI header under include/. This is the
# bootstrap consumed by setup.sh and `andesim build --what driver` (wired in
# F14). Out-of-tree build under build/driver; the binary is redirected to
# build/andesim via CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build/driver"

cmake -S "$ROOT/driver" -B "$BUILD" \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY="$ROOT/build" \
  >/dev/null

cmake --build "$BUILD" -j"$(nproc)"

echo "built: $ROOT/build/andesim"
----BUILD_ALL----
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# build_all.sh -- build the andesim artifacts. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim build` subcommand (which moved out of the driver
# binary). It only orchestrates the existing build scripts / Makefiles; the
# build logic itself lives in setup.sh, scripts/build_*.sh, and the Makefiles.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/build_all.sh [TARGET] [--dry-run]
#
# TARGET (default: all):
#   all       setup.sh (locate external qemu + vsim + plugin) then
#             fixtures (the fixtures Makefile also builds the runtime lib too)
#   plugin    qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
#   fixtures  tests/fixtures/*.elf (+ runtime lib)
#   runtime   build/runtime/ (rv64) + build/runtime/rv32/ (rv32, when
#             HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set): libandesim_runtime.a, crt0.o,
#             andesim.ld, andesim.specs, include/andesim/ROI.h
#
# --dry-run prints the underlying commands without running them.
#
# The andesim driver itself is NOT built here: ./andesim self-bootstraps via
# scripts/build_driver.sh on first use.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

TARGET=all
DRY_RUN=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    all|plugin|fixtures|runtime) TARGET="$arg" ;;
    *)
      echo "build_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: build_all.sh [all|plugin|fixtures|runtime] [--dry-run]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done

# run one step: print it under --dry-run, otherwise banner + execute (inheriting
# stdio so the user watches the build live). set -e aborts on the first failure.
run() {
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$*"
    return
  fi
  printf '[build_all] %s\n' "$*"
  "$@"
}

# plugin: build_qemu_plugin.sh wraps `make -C qemu_plugin`; plugins build against
# the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h (no QEMU source tree needed).
case "$TARGET" in
  all)      run bash "$ROOT/setup.sh"; run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  plugin)   run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_qemu_plugin.sh" ;;
  fixtures) run make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" ;;
  runtime)  run bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_runtime.sh" ;;
esac
----TEST_ALL----
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# test_all.sh -- run the full andesim test surface. This is the entry point that
# replaced the former `andesim test` subcommand (which moved out of the binary).
#
# Phases (all run, in order, unless named explicitly):
#   unit      build/driver/andesim-*-test   the C++ driver unit tests
#   contract  tests/andes_sim/*.sh          driver feature + parity contracts
#   e2e       scripts/run_e2e.sh            hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]
#
# --dry-run prints the plan without executing (and without building). The
# contract and e2e phases need built artifacts -- run scripts/build_all.sh
# first. FILTER / MODE / JOBS pass through to scripts/run_e2e.sh unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

DRY_RUN=0
PHASES=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    unit|contract|e2e) PHASES+=("$arg") ;;
    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

pass=0
failed=0
declare -a FAILED_NAMES=()

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return
  fi
  if ! bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null; then
    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature + parity contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/parity.sh" "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)" \
      "tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh (each)" "tests/engines/test_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi
  local s
  for s in "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/parity.sh "$ROOT"/tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh \
           "$ROOT"/tests/andes_csr/test_*.sh "$ROOT"/tests/engines/test_*.sh; do
    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;
  esac
done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo
  echo "(dry-run: nothing executed)"
  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

#
#   1. scripts/build_driver.sh builds build/andesim (executable).

#   3. andesim -h prints usage and exits zero.

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || fail "-h exit code should be 0, got $rc"
echo "$out" | grep -qi "usage" || fail "-h output missing 'usage':"$'\n'"$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 contract: CLI selection axes + `--` passthrough split + `list`.
#
#   1. list fixtures byte-matches the Python golden (hsim).
#   2. list models names the three models (fast/cycle/hybrid).
#   3. list engines scaffold exits 0 (populated in F2).
#   4. parse_cli unit tests pass (selection axes + `--` passthrough).

ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2 contract: engine registry + self-describe (the plugin + hot-plug query).
#
#   1. JSON parser unit tests pass.
#   2. the built-in qemu engine is always listed.
#   3. a self-describing engine in the scan dir is discovered (--describe).
#   4. its kind / vlen show in `list engines` (triggers are a hybrid-model
#      option, not an engine column).
#   5. HOT-PLUG: dropping a second engine in makes it appear with no rebuild.
#   6. SIDECAR fallback: a binary lacking --describe is read from <bin>.json.
#
# Discovery is exercised hermetically via ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR (which REPLACES
# the default verilator/build scan), so the real multi-MB sim binaries are
# never executed here.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
JSONTEST="$ROOT/build/driver/andesim-json-test"

bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing executable: $BIN"

# 1. JSON parser unit tests
[ -x "$JSONTEST" ] || fail "missing json unit-test binary: $JSONTEST"
"$JSONTEST" >/dev/null || fail "json unit tests failed"

# A self-describing fake engine: emits a descriptor on --describe, else fails.
make_engine() {  # $1=path  $2=id  $3=vlen  [$4=dlen  $5=elen]
  cat > "$1" <<OUTER
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "\$1" = "--describe" ]; then
  printf '%s\n' '{"id":"$2","type":"vsim","kind":"cycle-accurate","vlen":$3,"dlen":${4:-0},"elen":${5:-0},"xlen":64,"triggers":["marker","pc"],"roles":["standalone","accurate-leg"],"state":["resume","drain"],"invoke":{"standalone":["{bin}","{elf}"]},"result":"stderr:cycles"}'
  exit 0
fi
exit 1
OUTER
  chmod +x "$1"
}

ENGDIR=$(mktemp -d -t andes-f2.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$ENGDIR"' EXIT

make_engine "$ENGDIR/sim_fakeA" "vsim:fakeA" 256 192 32

# 2 + 3 + 4: qemu built-in present; fakeA discovered with its fields
out=$(ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR="$ENGDIR" "$BIN" list engines 2>/dev/null) \
  || fail "list engines exited non-zero"

# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu64`, `qemu32`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
`vsim:ax66_makatau`, and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`,
`sid`, or anything else. Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "dlen":     512,
  "elen":     32,
  "xlen":     64,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "andes_csrs": ["mxstatus", "mclk_ctl", "milmb", "mdlmb", "uitb", "jvt"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `dlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `DLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `elen`     | number          | no       | RVV `ELEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`, `doctor`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

### Roles

- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `cycle` models).
  Transparent passthrough: `andesim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
  the reported cycle figure.

### invoke + placeholders

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
tokens when it builds the command:

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
| `{mmap_size}` | the shared-mmap size in bytes |
| `{mmap_base}` | the guest physical base address of the mmap (e.g. `0x0`) |
| `{vlen}`      | the synced VLEN (bits) from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor |
| `{plugin}`    | the TCG plugin path (fast-leg only) |
| `{trigger}`   | the plugin comma-suffix for the trigger (e.g. `,enter_pc=0xADDR` for pc; empty for marker) |

`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
appended.

### result

Declares where an engine's standalone measurement lives. `stderr:<word>`
advertises that the figure is the integer next to `<word>` on stderr (vsim
prints `<n> cycles simulated`); `state.mcycle` advertises the `mcycle` field of
the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.

NOTE: the current driver does not yet act on this field. Standalone runs
(`fast`/`cycle`) pass the engine's stdout/stderr/exit code through verbatim, and
hybrid runs always read the cycle figure as the accurate-leg `mcycle` delta from
the drained state files. The field is parsed into the descriptor for forward
compatibility, not consumed.

## 2. ABI conformance

Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.

## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)

`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
shares it:

1. The built-in `qemu64` (rv64) and `qemu32` (rv32) descriptors are always
   present (QEMU does not implement `--describe`; their binary paths honor
   `$VSIM_QEMU` / `$VSIM_QEMU32`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
2. The scan directory is:
   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.

Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.

## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)

1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
4. **(Optional) GDB support**: `andesim run --mode cycle --gdb [--gdb-port N]` injects `--jtag-port <N>` (default 9104) into the engine argv before the user passthrough, then exec-replaces itself with ICEman (`$ICEMAN`). If your engine supports a JTAG bitbang port, implement `--jtag-port` to match vsim's interface. If it does not, the framework still builds the argv correctly -- the engine will simply ignore or reject the flag.
5. **(Optional) QEMU ISA match**: implement `--print-qemu-config` to emit a QEMU `-readconfig` cfg (per-extension `[global]` properties) describing your engine's ISA, so a hybrid run's QEMU fast leg executes the same extensions you model. On a hybrid run the framework runs `<accurate-engine> --print-qemu-config` and passes the result to QEMU via `-readconfig`. If you do not implement it (the flag exits non-zero), the framework falls back to QEMU's default `-cpu` -- no error. vsim bakes this cfg from its `config.inc` at build time (`docs/qemu_match_ROADMAP.md`).

    *)
      echo "test_all.sh: unknown argument: $arg" >&2
      echo "usage: test_all.sh [--dry-run] [unit|contract|e2e ...]" >&2
      exit 2
      ;;
  esac
done
[ "${#PHASES[@]}" -eq 0 ] && PHASES=(unit contract e2e)

step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\033[1;31m[FAIL]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

failed=0

# run_case NAME CMD...  -- execute one case, tally it, dump its log on failure.
run_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "$name"; return; fi
  local log rc; log=$(mktemp)
  "$@" >"$log" 2>&1; rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "$name"; pass=$((pass + 1))
  else
    fail "$name (rc=$rc)"; failed=$((failed + 1)); FAILED_NAMES+=("$name")
    cat "$log"
  fi
  rm -f "$log"
}

run_unit() {
  step "[unit] C++ driver unit tests"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "scripts/build_driver.sh" "build/driver/andesim-*-test (each)"
    return

    fail "[unit] build_driver.sh failed"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  shopt -s nullglob
  local bins=("$ROOT"/build/driver/andesim-*-test)
  shopt -u nullglob
  if [ "${#bins[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
    fail "[unit] no unit-test binaries under build/driver"; failed=$((failed + 1)); return
  fi
  local t
  for t in "${bins[@]}"; do run_case "[unit] $(basename "$t")" "$t"; done
}

run_contract() {
  step "[contract] driver feature contracts"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
    printf '  %s\n' "tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh (each)"
    return
  fi

    [ -f "$s" ] || continue
    run_case "[contract] $(basename "$s")" bash "$s"
  done
}

run_e2e() {
  step "[e2e] hybrid qemu+vsim round-trips"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then printf '  %s\n' "scripts/run_e2e.sh"; return; fi
  run_case "[e2e] run_e2e.sh" bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh"
}

for p in "${PHASES[@]}"; do
  case "$p" in
    unit)     run_unit ;;
    contract) run_contract ;;
    e2e)      run_e2e ;;

done

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = 1 ]; then
  echo

  exit 0
fi

echo
step "summary: $pass passed, $failed failed"
if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
  fail "failed: ${FAILED_NAMES[*]}"
  exit 1
fi

# Engine interface

How a simulator joins the `andesim` framework.

`andesim` drives several simulator backends behind one CLI. An **engine** is
one simulator *process* the framework can run: `qemu`, `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`,
and -- if they implement this interface -- `alioth`, `sid`, or anything else.
Engines are **drop-in binaries, not linked libraries**:
the framework is never recompiled to add one. Everything `andesim` needs to
know about an engine comes back from a single `--describe` call, so there is
zero per-engine code in the framework.

To join, an engine does two things:

1. **Self-describe** -- answer `--describe` with one JSON object (below).
2. **Speak the ABI** for any role it claims that moves architectural state
   (`resume` / `drain`): read/write `struct hybrid_state_v1`
   (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) byte-for-byte. A functional-only engine that
   only ever runs standalone needs none of this.

## 1. The `--describe` JSON

Running `<engine-binary> --describe` must print one JSON object to **stdout**
and exit 0. Example (Verilator):

```json
{
  "id":       "verilator:ax45mpv_premium",
  "type":     "verilator",
  "kind":     "cycle-accurate",
  "vlen":     512,
  "xlen":     64,
  "triggers": ["csr", "pc"],
  "roles":    ["standalone", "accurate-leg"],
  "state":    ["resume", "drain"],
  "invoke": {
    "standalone":   ["{bin}", "{elf}"],
    "accurate-leg": ["{bin}", "{elf}",
                     "--resume-from-qemu", "{state_in}",
                     "--handoff-out", "{state_out}",
                     "--shared-mem-path", "{mmap}",
                     "--shared-mem-size", "{mmap_size}",
                     "--shared-mem-base", "{mmap_base}"]
  },
  "result":   "stderr:cycles"
}
```

The framework silently normalizes the discovered descriptor: type `verilator` → `vsim`, and id `verilator:<cfg>` → `vsim:<cfg>`. Users see and pass the normalized form (e.g. `--engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium`). A non-Verilator engine (alioth, sid) that sets a different `type` passes through untouched.

### Fields

| Field      | Type            | Required | Meaning |
|------------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `id`       | string          | yes      | Unique engine id. Convention: `verilator:<cfg>`, `alioth`, `sid`. First id wins on a collision. |
| `type`     | string          | yes      | Family: `qemu` \| `verilator` \| `alioth` \| `sid` \| ... |
| `kind`     | string          | no       | `functional` or `cycle-accurate`. Shown by `list engines`. |
| `vlen`     | number          | no       | RVV `VLEN` in bits (0 / omit if no V). |
| `xlen`     | number          | no       | 32 or 64. |
| `triggers` | array\<string\> | no       | ROI delimiters the engine understands: `marker` \| `pc`. The Verilator engine reports the marker trigger under its legacy wire name `csr` (the example above emits `["csr", "pc"]`); unlike `type`/`id`, the framework does **not** normalize this array, so it is stored and shown (`list engines`) verbatim. The array is informational only -- it is never matched against the requested `--trigger`. |
| `roles`    | array\<string\> | no       | `standalone` \| `fast-leg` \| `accurate-leg` (see below). |
| `state`    | array\<string\> | no       | `hybrid_state_v1` capabilities: `resume`, `drain`. Omit if none. |
| `invoke`   | object          | no       | Per-role argv template (see Placeholders). |
| `result`   | string          | no       | Where the measurement is: `stderr:<word>` or `state.mcycle`. |

The parser is strict JSON (no comments, no trailing commas). Numbers are read
as integers. Unknown fields are ignored, so the schema can grow.

### Roles

- `standalone` -- run a whole program alone (the `fast` and `cycle` models).
  Transparent passthrough: `andesim` forwards the user's post-`--` args
  verbatim and the engine's own stdout/stderr/exit code is the result.
- `fast-leg` -- the QEMU fast-forward leg of a `hybrid` run: execute up to the
  ROI entry, then **drain** `hybrid_state_v1`.
- `accurate-leg` -- the cycle-accurate leg of a `hybrid` run: **resume** from a
  drained state, execute the ROI, then **drain** again. Its `mcycle` delta is
  the reported cycle figure.

### invoke + placeholders

`invoke` maps a role to its argv template. The framework substitutes these
tokens when it builds the command:

| Placeholder   | Filled with |
|---------------|-------------|
| `{bin}`       | the engine binary path |
| `{elf}`       | the workload ELF |
| `{state_in}`  | the input state file (resume) |
| `{state_out}` | the output state file (drain) |
| `{mmap}`      | the shared-memory backing file |
| `{mmap_size}` | the shared-mmap size in bytes |
| `{mmap_base}` | the guest physical base address of the mmap (e.g. `0x0`) |
| `{vlen}`      | the synced VLEN (bits) from the accurate-leg engine's descriptor |
| `{plugin}`    | the TCG plugin path (fast-leg only) |
| `{trigger}`   | the plugin comma-suffix for the trigger (e.g. `,enter_pc=0xADDR` for pc; empty for marker) |

`standalone` typically needs only `["{bin}", "{elf}"]`; the user's `--` args are
appended.

### result

Declares where an engine's standalone measurement lives. `stderr:<word>`
advertises that the figure is the integer next to `<word>` on stderr (vsim
prints `<n> cycles simulated`); `state.mcycle` advertises the `mcycle` field of
the drained `hybrid_state_v1`.

NOTE: the current driver does not yet act on this field. Standalone runs
(`fast`/`cycle`) pass the engine's stdout/stderr/exit code through verbatim, and
hybrid runs always read the cycle figure as the accurate-leg `mcycle` delta from
the drained state files. The field is parsed into the descriptor for forward
compatibility, not consumed.

## 2. ABI conformance

Any engine listing `resume` or `drain` in `state` must exchange architectural
state through `struct hybrid_state_v1` exactly as defined in
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, and the V block;
little-endian; `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128`). V data registers travel through
the shared-memory scratch region by the convention the header documents. An
engine that only claims `standalone` (no `state`) is exempt.

## Discovery (how the framework finds engines)

`andesim list engines` performs discovery; every other engine-using command
shares it:

1. The built-in `qemu` descriptor is always present (QEMU does not implement
   `--describe`; its binary path honors `$VSIM_QEMU`, then `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`).
2. The scan directory is:
   - `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` if set (colon-separated; **replaces** the default
     and accepts **any** executable -- this is where you drop `alioth` / `sid`),
   - otherwise `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (the external prebuilt vsim build dir, mirroring
     `$QEMU_BIN_DIR`; falls back to the legacy in-tree `<repo>/verilator/build`
     when unset), filtered to `sim_*` binaries.
3. For each candidate binary the framework runs `<bin> --describe`. If that
   fails (non-zero, hang past a 5 s timeout, or non-JSON) it falls back to a
   sidecar file `<bin>.json` containing the same descriptor -- the escape hatch
   for binaries that cannot add the flag.
4. Descriptors are deduped by `id`.

Because discovery is pure runtime scan + self-describe, **building a new
Verilator config and dropping `sim_<cfg>` into the scan dir makes it appear with
no `andesim` rebuild.** That is the hot-plug guarantee.

## Joining as a new engine (alioth / sid)

1. Implement `--describe` to print the JSON above (set `id`, `type`, `kind`,
   the roles you support, and `invoke` templates for those roles). If you cannot
   add the flag, ship a `<bin>.json` sidecar instead.
2. If you claim `resume`/`drain`, read/write `hybrid_state_v1` per
   `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`.
3. Put the binary on `$ANDESIM_ENGINES_DIR` and run `andesim list engines`
   to confirm it shows up. Done -- no framework change required.
